stories.headline: Pakistan refused to accept bodies of its own soldiers killed in Kargil war: India at UN
stories.title: Pakistan refused to accept bodies of its own soldiers killed in Kargil war: India at UN
stories.summary: United Nations, Oct 23: India slammed Pakistan at the UN, reminding the country that it did not even accept the bodies of its own soldiers killed in combat in the 1999 Kargil war but speaks about faith, religious freedom and burials. The interim report of the Special Rapporteur on freedom of religion and belief, Nazila Ghanea, said that "Reports of systemic denial of funeral rights in the context of individuals killed in security operations in Jammu and Kashmir, India, including denial of return of bodies to families and remote and secret burials, disproportionately affecting Muslims and notably inconsistent with their practices, raise serious concerns.” "It is deeply ironic that a State that did not even accept the bodies of its own soldiers who were killed in combat in 1999 in Kargil unabashedly speaks with fervor on faith, religious freedom, and burials,” First Secretary at the Permanent Mission of India to the UN Bhavika Mangalanandan said here Thursday, a strong reference to Pakistan. Indian Army recovered bodies of Pakistani soldiers who died in the Kargil War and provided them with burials after Pakistan refused to acknowledge the involvement of Pakistan Army personnel in the war. Addressing the interactive dialogue with the Special Rapporteur on freedom of religion and belief on the topic of funeral rights in exceptional circumstances, Mangalanandan reminded Pakistan that it was the Indian Army that buried several Pakistani soldiers with military honours and in accordance with Islamic rights. “Pakistan's deep obsession with what is happening in the Indian Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir should be actually directed at the developments that are underway in the parts of Jammu and Kashmir under its illegal occupation, such as Rawalakot,” she said, adding that in Pakistan, a number of minorities are shrinking; their rights regularly abused. “A State that cannot ensure the safety of its own minorities has no standing to lecture India,” she said. Mangalanandan added that burial rights for terrorists are being justified by indicating that States may restrict funeral rights of terrorists, but only within legal limits. “Legal limits should be determined in accordance with the principles of sovereign rights. A terrorist not only kills innocent people but damages the psyche of a nation,” she said, adding that the report’s fervent advocacy for the rights of terrorists, who violate the most sacred right of humans - the right to life - does not similarly extend to the victims of terrorism. “The report goes back half a decade to find references to my country. It fails when it comes to grave violations committed recently in our region and in the developed world,” she said. Mangalanandan said that as per the report, all discrimination and wrong practices during COVID-19 supposedly took place only in the Global South. “What benefit does the report derive by not mentioning similar tragic situations in the developed world? Deriving political mileage out of people's pain and loss should not be a topic that SRs (Special Rapporteurs) should base their relevance on,” she said.

stories.headline: Earthquake of Magnitude 7.0 Strikes Tibet; 16 Dead, 32 injured
stories.title: Earthquake of Magnitude 7.0 Strikes Tibet; 16 Dead, 32 injured
stories.summary: Tibet, October 23 : At least 16 people have died and 32 others have been injured after a magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck Tibet on Thursday, Chinese state news agency Xinhua reported. According to the United States Geological Survey (USGS), the epicentre was located 183 km east-northeast of Nagqu city in Tibet. As per Xinhua, more than 300 houses have collapsed in the affected region, while the full extent of the damage is still being assessed. Rescue teams have been dispatched to the affected areas to carry out relief and rescue operations. Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported that railway authorities have suspended train services through the quake-hit areas following the earthquake. The National Centre for Seismology (NCS) on X stated, “The quake occurred at 20:03:43 IST at a depth of 173 km, with its epicentre at latitude 32.368 N and longitude 93.853 E, according to the NCS.” According to Xinhua's latest report published today, 11 of the 32 injured people were in serious condition, while 21 sustained minor injuries, as of 2:25 am (local time). More than 300 houses had collapsed in the affected region. The regional emergency command centre in Xizang has activated a Level-II emergency response to the earthquake to expedite rescue and relief operations in the affected areas. Further details are awaited.

A magnitude-7.0 earthquake struck Tibet on Thursday, killing 16 people and injuring 32 others.
More than 300 houses collapsed, prompting rescue and relief operations.
Officials are assessing the damage as the region faces renewed concerns over disaster vulnerability.

Beijing, Oct 23: A magnitude 7 earthquake hit China's Tibet region on Thursday evening, killing at least 16 people, injuring 54 and collapsing hundreds of homes in the northern regional city of Nagqu, official media said.
Search and rescue efforts continued following the collapse of at least 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds, the Nagqu media office said, citing city government officials.
More than 1,600 people from the local county were deployed for rescue efforts.
Supplies including 1,000 prefabricated housing units, around 3,000 tents and folding beds, as well as flashlights and winter clothing arrived in the region.

The US Geological Survey said the quake occurred at 10:33 pm local time, with its epicentre 191 kilometres (119 miles) east-northeast of Nagqu, in a sparsely populated, high-altitude area of northern Tibet.
The US agency recorded at least seven aftershocks with magnitude between 4.3 and 5.2, all of them with a depth of 10 kilometres (six miles), according to its website.
China's official news agency Xinhua said on Friday that communication in part of the region has been down.
Local railway authorities have taken emergency actions to halt trains passing through the region.

The earthquake also caused rockfalls that have forced local authorities to close a section of National Highway 317, allowing only emergency, rescue and official support vehicles through as crews worked to clear debris, according to Xinhua.
It was the biggest earthquake in the region in the last five years, China's national broadcaster CCTV said.
Chinese President Xi Jinping called for all-out efforts in rescue operations and medical relief work.

stories.headline: Bay of Bengal Low-Pressure System Likely to Become Cyclone by Oct. 26
stories.title: Bay of Bengal Low-Pressure System Likely to Become Cyclone by Oct. 26
stories.summary: IMD forecasts intensification into a depression on October 24 and a deep depression on October 25, prompting Odisha to begin precautionary preparations.
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 2 independent source groups -> high confidence
article_sentences: The Bay of Bengal is brewing a potentially powerful cyclone, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) hinting at its formation by Monday as a parent low-pressure area emerged over the south-east and adjoining east-central Bay on Friday morning.
The system is expected to move west-north-westwards, intensify into a deep depression by Sunday, and become a cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay by Monday morning.
It is then forecast to strengthen further and head towards the north Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts over the next two days.
Global models suggest it could reach at least severe cyclonic storm intensity.
Meanwhile, another low-pressure area is holding sway over the south-east Arabian Sea, off the south Kerala coast, setting the stage for an intriguing interaction between the two systems.
The European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts had suggested last week that the Arabian Sea low and the developing Bay cyclone could feed off each other, helping both systems strengthen.
Under that scenario, the Bay system would approach the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha coast, while its Arabian Sea counterpart would move northwards along the Kerala-Karnataka coast towards Goa.
The IMD, however, envisages a different twist to the tale.

Strong south-westerly flows feeding the systems could steer the Arabian Sea low back across the South Peninsula towards the south-west Bay, close to south Tamil Nadu and north Sri Lanka, from where it originated.
Thereafter, it could merge with the developing cyclone over the larger Bay.
Such a convergence could give the north-east monsoon another powerful burst next week, keeping the Southern Peninsula firmly in the rain belt even as the Bay system gathers strength.
Another rain-bearing system is in the forecast as Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal recover impressively from a distressing south-west monsoon season between June and September.

stories.headline: UN climate fund provisionally earmarks $20 million for flood-hit Nepal
stories.title: UN climate fund provisionally earmarks $20 million for flood-hit Nepal
stories.summary: UN climate fund provisionally earmarks US$20 million for Nepal’s flood recovery
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The UN’s Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD) has provisionally set aside US$20 million for Nepal following devastating floods in August, offering limited financial support as the country faces a multibillion-dollar recovery bill.
The decision was taken at an extraordinary meeting of the fund’s board on Thursday.
Nepal will still have to submit a funding application, which the board is expected to consider at its next meeting in December.

Nepal’s Ministry of Agriculture, Forests and Environment described the decision as approval of assistance worth approximately NPR 3 billion for relief, rehabilitation and reconstruction in affected communities.
The 26 August disaster struck the Bhotekoshi–Trishuli region, triggering floods and landslides that caused extensive destruction.
According to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, more than 1,400 people were killed and over 5,000 remained unaccounted for.
Preliminary estimates indicated that around 60,000 people across 15,000 households were directly affected.
Assessments cited in the reports put economic losses and damage at between US$2.56 billion and US$2.69 billion, with recovery and reconstruction requirements estimated at US$4.71 billion.
The proposed funding would therefore meet less than 1 per cent of the estimated losses.
Agriculture, Forests and Environment Minister Gita Chaudhary and Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle had jointly written to the fund on 31 August, requesting urgent assistance.
Several rounds of consultations involving representatives of developed and developing countries followed.

Raju Pandit Chhetri, lead climate finance negotiator for the least-developed countries at the UN climate negotiations, welcomed the decision as evidence that international cooperation could deliver a timely response to vulnerable countries.

stories.title: ITBP has raised drone platoons, building bunkers along LAC, says DG
stories.summary: The ITBP has raised drone platoons in all its border units, prepared a new 'Strike' course to better handle Galwan-like battles and is creating underground infrastructure along the front "in a big way" as part of the new warfare to counter India's "biggest adversary" China, the force's chief said on Thursday. ITBP Director General (DG) Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor told his troops at a force base in Rajasthan's Alwar that countering China through "traditional" means of warfare was a thing of the past and hence they were investing in modernizing the force, its weapons, vehicles and border posts. The Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), raised in 1962, guards the 3,488-km-long Line of Actual Control (LAC) with China. The DG noted that the recent Ukraine-Russia and Iran-US wars have shown the importance of drone and anti-drone technology through which a small country can overwhelm a bigger nation during conflict. Kapoor, who is set to retire from service on October 31, addressed his troops ..

stories.headline: Cabinet Secretariat took no action on 2 Election Commissioners’ complaints against EC officer: RTI
stories.title: Cabinet Secretariat took no action on 2 Election Commissioners’ complaints against EC officer: RTI
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The complaints alleged that Maneesh Garg changed work allocations among senior poll officials without prior consultation or approval from the Election Commission.

New Delhi: The Cabinet Secretariat took no action on complaints sent by two Election Commissioners against the conduct of an officer in the Election Commission of India (ECI), stating that the communications were made in their “individual capacity” and that action without an official communication from the Commission as a whole could be inappropriate, documents released under the Right to Information (RTI) Act show.

Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had sent separate communications on July 29 to Cabinet Secretary T.V. Somanathan, raising concerns about the working of Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Maneesh Garg, an IAS officer posted to the Commission by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) on September 2, 2024.
The letters were provided in an RTI response to activist Commodore Lokesh K. Batra (retd).

The Indian Express had reported in September that Sandhu and Joshi wrote to the Cabinet Secretary after a work allocation order within the poll body raised concerns about the centralisation of powers to add or delete names and update records in electoral rolls, instead of allowing officials at the state level to handle these tasks.
In a statement on September 26, the Election Commission said the work redistribution orders issued by Garg had not been implemented following directions from the two Commissioners.
The poll panel also said the letters to the Cabinet Secretary concerned an officer on deputation, rather than policy or information technology division matters.
What did the Commissioners allege?

According to a Cabinet note included in the RTI response, both Commissioners alleged that Garg, after assuming charge as link officer of the Deputy Election Commissioner (Administration), issued an order changing work allocations among officers of equivalent or higher rank without consulting the Commission or the officers concerned.
They said the move came despite repeated oral and written instructions against making such changes without prior discussion or approval of the Commission.
The Commissioners alleged that Garg’s actions violated the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.
Joshi also said that when he sought the relevant file from the Administration Division, it was not provided to him.

stories.headline: Tibet hit by 7.0-magnitude quake, leaving 16 dead and 32 injured
stories.title: Tibet hit by 7.0-magnitude quake, leaving 16 dead and 32 injured
stories.summary: Lhasa, Oct 23 : Sixteen people were killed and 32 others injured after a 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck Tibet on Thursday, according to the city's emergency management bureau. As of 2:25 a.m. Friday, 11 of the injured were in serious condition while 21 sustained minor injuries. Over 300 houses collapsed. The damage caused by the quake is being further evaluated, and disaster relief work is underway, reports Xinhua news agency. More than 300 police officers have been dispatched to the epicenter for relief work while the regional fire and rescue corps has mobilised 347 personnel to the affected areas. The latest earthquake also follows seismic activity recorded in Tibet on September 3, when a magnitude 5.0 earthquake struck at a depth of approximately 14 kilometres. In January 2025, another major earthquake measuring 6.8, according to the China Earthquake Networks Centre, killed more than 120 people and injured hundreds. According to India’s National Centre for Seismology (NCS), the earthquake occurred at a depth of 173 kilometres below the Earth’s surface. The epicentre was approximately 400 kilometres from Lhasa, the Tibetan capital. Experts have warned that rising temperatures, retreating glaciers and increasingly extreme weather events could heighten natural disaster risks across the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. Experts say that the latest earthquake has renewed attention on the region’s vulnerability as communities continue to grapple with the consequences of recent disasters. The earthquake has come weeks after an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26 triggered catastrophic flash floods. The floods swept away homes, roads and bridges, damaged hydropower projects, and left thousands of people missing, causing widespread destruction across the affected areas. The earthquakes come weeks after devastating flash floods earlier in August this year which killed over 1,400 people in the Nepal-Tibet border region in August. The deadly floods originated near the Nepal-Tibet border. --IANS

stories.headline: HPCL refinances Rs 50,000 crore refinery debt
stories.title: HPCL refinances Rs 50,000 crore refinery debt
stories.summary: New Delhi: Hindustan Petroleum Corp. (HPCL) has refinanced about Rs 50,000 crore of debt at its Rajasthan refinery, securing a reduction of around 105 basis points in borrowing costs and targeting annual interest savings of about Rs 1,000 crore through a broader restructuring of the project's finances, Chairman and Managing Director Vikas Kaushal said on Friday.The refinancing, effective October 3, is expected to save the company about Rs 470 crore to Rs 550 crore annually, Kaushal told analysts on an earnings call.Additional equity infusions, conversion of subordinated loans into equity and interest-free state support are expected to further ease the refinery's financing burden as HPCL ramps up operations at the facility.The 9 million tonnes a year refinery in Rajasthan was built at a cost of Rs 79,459 crore, with HPCL (74 per cent) and Government of Rajasthan (26 per cent) as equity partners.HPCL Rajasthan Refinery Limited (HRRL), the joint venture company, part refinanced existing project loans through Rs 8,000 crore in rupee term loans from a consortium comprising the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID), India Infrastructure Finance Company Limited (IIFCL), ICICI Bank Limited, UCO Bank and Punjab & Sind Bank; a Rs 2,000 crore working capital demand loan from Bank of Baroda; and fund-based and non-fund-based credit facilities aggregating to Rs 400 crore from ICICI Bank Limited.The term loan proceeds will be utilised for the part refinancing of existing project loans, while the working capital facilities will support HRRL's working capital requirements and help address cash flow mismatches associated with the project, including its allied utilities and facilities at Pachpadra, District Balotra, Rajasthan.Kaushal said the financial restructuring is aimed at improving the economics of the Rajasthan refinery, a major new asset that HPCL expects to bring towards full operating capacity by December. The company is also working to stabilise its other complex refining assets and contain costs as volatile crude prices and rising losses on domestic cooking gas threaten near-term earnings."We have significantly altered the debt structure of the company," he said, adding that the refinancing and other measures could reduce annual interest costs by about Rs 1,000 crore compared with the previous year.The Rajasthan government infused Rs 1,500 crore of equity into the refinery during the September quarter, while HPCL converted Rs 4,300 crore of subordinated loans into equity, Kaushal said. opening: (HPCL) has refinanced about Rs 50,000 crore of debt at its Rajasthan refinery, securing a reduction of around 105 basis points in borrowing costs and targeting annual interest savings of about Rs 1,000 crore through a broader restructuring of the project's finances, Chairman and Managing Director Vikas Kaushal said on Friday.
body: Additional equity infusions, conversion of subordinated loans into equity and interest-free state support are expected to further ease the refinery's financing burden as HPCL ramps up operations at the facility.
The 9 million tonnes a year refinery in Rajasthan was built at a cost of Rs 79,459 crore, with HPCL (74 per cent) and Government of Rajasthan (26 per cent) as equity partners.

HPCL Rajasthan Refinery Limited (HRRL), the joint venture company, part refinanced existing project loans through Rs 8,000 crore in rupee term loans from a consortium comprising the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID), India Infrastructure Finance Company Limited (IIFCL), ICICI Bank Limited, UCO Bank and Punjab & Sind Bank; a Rs 2,000 crore working capital demand loan from Bank of Baroda; and fund-based and non-fund-based credit facilities aggregating to Rs 400 crore from ICICI Bank Limited.

The term loan proceeds will be utilised for the part refinancing of existing project loans, while the working capital facilities will support HRRL's working capital requirements and help address cash flow mismatches associated with the project, including its allied utilities and facilities at Pachpadra, District Balotra, Rajasthan.
Kaushal said the financial restructuring is aimed at improving the economics of the Rajasthan refinery, a major new asset that HPCL expects to bring towards full operating capacity by December.

The company is also working to stabilise its other complex refining assets and contain costs as volatile crude prices and rising losses on domestic cooking gas threaten near-term earnings." We have significantly altered the debt structure of the company," he said, adding that the refinancing and other measures could reduce annual interest costs by about Rs 1,000 crore compared with the previous year.
The Rajasthan government infused Rs 1,500 crore of equity into the refinery during the September quarter, while HPCL converted Rs 4,300 crore of subordinated loans into equity, Kaushal said.
The conversion is expected to lower interest costs by about Rs 350 crore.
Further equity calls are planned over the next one or two quarters.
The state has also committed to providing about Rs 1,100 crore annually in interest-free loans, with the first instalment already received, according to Kaushal.
HPCL is seeking to improve the refinery's financial performance as it moves beyond commissioning and begins shipping substantial volumes of products.
The facility's commercial operation date was declared on June 22 and it is currently running at about 60 per cent utilisation, broadly in line with earlier guidance.
Almost all secondary processing units are operating in hot circulation, with two units still to be brought into that state.
HPCL expects to complete the remaining commissioning work, including the sulphur recovery unit, before moving towards full-capacity operations.
The company expects throughput to reach a run rate of 8 million to 9 million tonnes per annum around December, give or take a week or two, Kaushal said.
The refinery recorded a gross refining margin of about USD 12 per barrel in the September quarter.
HPCL expects margins to rise above USD 20 per barrel in the fourth quarter as it transitions to processing higher-sulphur crude, which the facility is designed to handle.
Product shipments have already increased sharply.
Kaushal said the refinery shipped about 15,000 tonnes of products on the day before the call, compared with no shipments three months earlier.
October shipments are expected to exceed 400,000 tonnes, generating revenue of more than Rs 4,000 crore for the month.

Kaushal said the refinery could post a positive monthly profit before tax in October, although he stressed that this was an expression of management's optimism rather than formal guidance, given the volatility of refining margins and the early stage of operations." We are very excited on the Rajasthan.
We are very bullish on it," he said.
